questions.question: The gearshift lever is operated by:
questions.explanation: On a motorcycle, the gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: When stopping:

options.text: The rear brake should be applied first.
The front brake should be applied first.
Both brakes should be applied at the same time.
Only one brake, front or rear, should be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes should be applied at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is well-protected if they are wearing:

options.text: A jacket that allows the arms to be exposed.
Shoes that stop below their ankle.

questions.explanation: Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and give you a better grip on the controls. You should also wear a full jacket and pants, sturdy boots that cover your ankles, and low heels that won't catch on the pegs.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a way to prevent a friend from driving while intoxicated?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for them.
Get them involved in activities to slow their drinking and keep them busy while they sober up.
Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
Get other friends involved in stopping your friend from driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
questions.explanation: Waiting 15 minutes does not work. Instead, arrange a ride for them, keep them busy with other activities, use excuses to delay them, and ask other friends to help stop them from driving.

questions.question: You'll have a better chance of avoiding serious injury if you wear all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, sturdy jacket and pants, tall boots that cover your ankles, and durable gloves. Ear buds do not protect you in a crash.

questions.question: If the front wheel locks, you should:

options.text: Continue to hold the brake and the skid should end.
Release the front brake and not use the front brake.
Release the front brake and then quickly squeeze the front brake.
Release the front brake immediately and re-apply the front brake smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately and re-apply the front brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks up, release the front brake right away. Then apply the brake again slowly and gently.

questions.question: When should your rearview mirror be adjusted?
questions.explanation: Clean and adjust both mirrors before you start your motorcycle. Position them so you can see the lane behind you and the lane next to you.

questions.question: Riders who do not wear helmets while riding are ________ to die in a crash than riders who do wear helmets.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders who wear helmets.

questions.question: Which of the following provides a rider with the best protection?
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield and eyeglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, it is usually best to:

options.text: Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire fails, hold the handgrips firmly and slow down by easing off the throttle. If you must brake, gently apply the brake on the good tire. Edge slowly toward the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: Convex mirrors make cars look:
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road than flat mirrors. However, they make objects look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Usually, the best way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make things more dangerous. The tailgater may just continue tailgating at a higher speed.

questions.question: For eye or face shield protection to work well, it must be all of the following, except:

options.text: Too tight to allow sunglasses or eyeglasses to be worn.
Able to give clear views to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Too tight to allow sunglasses or eyeglasses to be worn.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be free of scratches, fasten securely, give clear views to both sides, prevent fogging, and allow room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used when you need to stop quickly.
Should be used only under slippery conditions.
Is not as effective as the rear brake.
Is safe to use if used properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe to use if used properly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It is safe to use if you use it the right way.

questions.question: The front brake provides how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders in groups communicate. When the lead rider extends their left arm straight down with palm facing back, it signals the group to stop.

questions.question: You should choose the lane position that can:

options.text: Reduce your space cushion and allow you to be seen by others.
Increase your space cushion and allow you to be seen by others.
Increase your chances of hitting road hazards and allow others to pass you.
Reduce your chances of hitting road hazards and allow you to closely follow another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your space cushion and allow you to be seen by others.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards on the road. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route. Choose a position that increases your space cushion.

questions.question: A driver making eye contact with you:

options.text: Does not mean that they will properly yield to you.
Guarantees that they will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean that they will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not count on eye contact to guarantee that a driver will yield. Drivers often look directly at a motorcyclist but do not actually notice them.

questions.question: To be seen in the rearview mirror of the driver ahead of you, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: When following a car, ride behind it in the center of your lane. This position puts you in the driver's rearview mirror. Most drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: Before you get on your motorcycle, your pre-ride inspection should include everything except:
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn. Do a complete inspection before you ride.

questions.question: A good face shield should not:
questions.explanation: A good face shield should have no scratches, stay clear, allow you to see to both sides, fasten tightly, and let air pass through. An airtight shield can fog up and make it hard to see.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle with a sidecar, the passenger should ride:

options.text: Either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.

questions.explanation: If your motorcycle has a sidecar, your passenger should ride in it. They should keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Keep riding and let it fix itself.
Ease off the throttle to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease off the throttle to slow down.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make wobbling worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slow down by closing the throttle gradually, lean your weight forward and down, and pull over as soon as you safely can. Then check what is causing the wobble.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If you can do it safely, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate you at a higher speed.
